evidence.source_name: Task Atlas AI2-THOR task proposals, round 2
evidence.scope: Proposed collection designs anchored to AI2-THOR / ProcTHOR asset-database object types, generated with claude-opus-5-5 from data/research/thor_candidates.json.
evidence.limitations: This design-seed source supports proposed task-suitability provenance only. AI2-THOR state flags describe the simulator's object model, not a physical product; they do not establish physical feasibility, population frequency, robot execution, or asset compatibility.
evidence.notes: Simulator state names (isOpen, isToggled, isDirty, isFilledWithLiquid, isSliced) are mapped to Atlas predicates in each task's notes.

external_objects.name_ja: AI2-THOR Fridge_1 大型冷蔵庫
external_objects.notes: AI2-THOR / ProcTHOR asset Fridge_1 of objectType Fridge. Asset-database state flags: primaryProperty Static; secondaryProperties Receptacle, CanOpen, isColdSource. AI2-THOR has no WordNet synsets, so source_taxonomy repeats the objectType as both category_id and synset_id. The asset ships inside the AI2-THOR Unity build with no per-object mesh download. The simulator's state model (boolean flags) does not establish how a physical product behaves, and does not establish compatibility with Task Atlas, another simulator, or a robot setup. The Atlas concept link object_kitchen_appliance is a curator grouping only. Bounding box about 1.01 m wide, 1.97 m tall, and 0.72 m deep closed (1.54 m deep in the database's open pose); split train. THOR models the door as one scripted isOpen boolean on a Static object, with no hinge or seal model, so physical collection needs a real refrigerator or an articulated refrigerator source (for example PartNet-Mobility). isColdSource cools items placed inside in simulation; that flag says nothing about a real appliance's temperature.

tasks.name_en: Shut the refrigerator door that was left ajar until it seals
tasks.name_ja: 半開きの冷蔵庫の扉をパッキンが密着するまで閉める
instruction_variants: The fridge door was left ajar; push it shut until the seal closes all the way round.
Close the refrigerator door properly so it isn't hanging open.
冷蔵庫の扉が少し開いたままです。パッキンが全周で密着するまで扉を閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one object, one goal predicate change (open -> closed), one uninterrupted push. THOR mapping: closed(thor_object_fridge_1) <-> Fridge isOpen=false; open <-> isOpen=true. THOR's Fridge is a Static object with one isOpen boolean and no seal model, and the asset's door count is not recorded in the database, so 'closed' is defined physically as every door of the unit sealed. clear(thor_resource_fridge_door_swing_path) is a setup precondition (nothing in the door's path or protruding from the shelves), not a goal. Physical collection needs a real refrigerator or an articulated refrigerator source; the door starts 30 +/- 5 degrees open so it cannot self-close.

tasks.name_ja: ボウルに置いた卵を割り、中身をボウル内に収める（シミュレーションのみ）
instruction_variants: Crack the egg that's sitting in the mixing bowl; keep all of it inside the bowl.
Break the egg in the bowl without knocking the bowl over or flicking anything out.
ボウルの中の卵を割ってください。中身も殻もボウルの外に出さないでください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one object, one goal predicate change (whole -> cracked); the egg starts and ends inside the bowl and the bowl stays upright, so both are preserved constraints. THOR mapping: cracked(thor_object_egg_1) <-> the Egg is replaced by an EggCracked object (Egg isSliced=true after SliceObject, or isBroken=true after BreakObject; which action is used must be confirmed in the simulator, see the planning condition); inside(...) <-> the EggCracked object's parentReceptacles contains the Bowl; whole <-> the Egg object still exists with isSliced=false and isBroken=false. Simulation-only: a raw egg is a hygiene hazard and a hollow shell surrogate does not model the contents, so no physical collection is proposed. Cracking an egg held over the bowl from the counter would add a second change (egg moved into the bowl) and would be compound; this task keeps the THOR in-place form. The bowl is a planning resource.

tasks.name_en: Switch off the coffee machine and leave the filled mug under the spout
tasks.name_ja: コーヒーメーカーの電源を切り、注がれたマグカップは抽出口の下に置いたままにする
instruction_variants: The coffee is done; switch the machine off and leave the mug where it is.
Turn off the coffee maker without moving the full mug under the spout.
コーヒーメーカーの電源を切ってください。抽出口の下のマグカップは動かさないでください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one goal predicate change on the machine (switched_on -> switched_off), one press. The mug's position and uprightness hold at both start and end, so they are preserved constraints; full(thor_object_mug_1) is a start condition only, and the goal does not require the mug to stay full because a spill is already a failure of upright or position. Cross-link: the mug is the thor_round1 ObjectInstance thor_object_mug_1. THOR mapping: switched_off(thor_object_coffee_machine_1) <-> CoffeeMachine isToggled=false; inside(thor_object_mug_1, thor_object_coffee_machine_1) <-> the Mug's parentReceptacles contains the CoffeeMachine (its ObjectSpecificReceptacle slot); full <-> Mug isFilledWithLiquid=true with fillLiquid=coffee in simulation. THOR toggles the machine object itself; real collection presses the physical power button, listed as a resource. Physical collection: the machine is unplugged and a battery dummy indicator wired to its power button stands in for power; the mug holds room-temperature water, not hot coffee.

tasks.name_en: Put the lettuce on the refrigerator's middle shelf and close the door
tasks.name_ja: レタスを冷蔵庫の中段の棚に入れて扉を閉める
instruction_variants: Put the head of lettuce on the fridge's middle shelf and shut the door.
Store the lettuce in the refrigerator, middle shelf, and make sure the door is closed after.
レタスを冷蔵庫の中段の棚に置き、扉をしっかり閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: one net change (the lettuce moves from the counter onto the middle shelf inside the fridge; inside and on_top_of describe the same placement) plus a transient articulation that must be reversed (door opened, then closed), over two objects in one sitting. closed(thor_object_fridge_1) holds at both start and end, so it is a preserved end-state constraint. refrigerated is not a goal: it takes time and is not observable at episode end. THOR mapping: inside(thor_object_lettuce_1, thor_object_fridge_1) <-> the Lettuce's parentReceptacles contains the Fridge; on_top_of(..., thor_resource_fridge_middle_shelf) <-> the Lettuce's parentReceptacles also contains the Fridge's middle shelf receptacle (THOR shelves are sub-receptacles of the Fridge; whether Fridge_1 exposes separate shelf receptacles must be confirmed, see the planning condition); closed <-> Fridge isOpen=false. Cross-link: the fridge is thor_object_fridge_1, the anchor of task_thor_r2_fridge_door_ajar_shut. Physical collection uses a real refrigerator and a whole lettuce head or a firm surrogate of the same size.

tasks.name_en: Fill the kettle with water to the fill band, shut its lid, and turn the faucet off
tasks.name_ja: やかんに目盛りまで水を入れ、蓋を閉めて蛇口を止める
instruction_variants: Fill the kettle at the sink up to the fill band, close the lid, turn the tap off, and put the kettle back on the counter.
Get the kettle filled with water, lid shut, and back in its spot; don't leave the water running.
やかんに流しで目盛りまで水を入れ、蓋を閉めて調理台の元の場所に戻してください。蛇口は必ず閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: one net change (empty -> filled_with_water on the kettle) plus two transient articulations that must be reversed (lid opened then closed; faucet on then off), over two objects in one sitting. closed(kettle), switched_off(faucet), and the counter position hold at both start and end, so they are preserved end-state constraints. Cross-link: the faucet is the thor_round1 ObjectInstance thor_object_kitchen_faucet_1. THOR mapping: filled_with_water(thor_object_kettle_1) <-> Kettle isFilledWithLiquid=true with fillLiquid=water; closed(thor_object_kettle_1) <-> Kettle isOpen=false (the asset's open pose raises only the lid); switched_off(thor_object_kitchen_faucet_1) <-> Faucet isToggled=false; the kettle fills in THOR when it sits under the running faucet, and whether it fills with its lid closed must be confirmed (see the planning condition), because the physical task needs the lid open. Physical 'filled' is a water level between the 0.5 L and 1.0 L marks read on the level window or with a marked dipstick; 1.0 L keeps kettle plus water under about 1.6 kg. Kettle_1 is a stovetop kettle, so no power isolation is needed; the stove is not used.

tasks.name_en: Slice the apple, put all the slices in the bowl, and put the knife back in its closed drawer
tasks.name_ja: りんごを切り分けて全部ボウルに入れ、包丁を引き出しに戻して閉める
instruction_variants: Take the knife from the drawer, cut the apple into slices, put every slice in the bowl, then put the knife back and shut the drawer.
Slice up the apple into the bowl and don't leave the knife out.
引き出しから包丁を出してりんごを切り分け、全部ボウルに入れてください。包丁は引き出しに戻して閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: two net changes on the apple (whole -> sliced; board -> bowl) plus a transient tool excursion that must be reversed (drawer opened, knife taken out and returned, drawer closed), over four objects in one sitting. The knife's place in the drawer and the closed drawer hold at both start and end, so they are preserved end-state constraints. THOR mapping: sliced(thor_object_apple_1) <-> Apple isSliced=true (SliceObject with a Knife held replaces the apple with AppleSliced pieces); inside(thor_object_apple_1, thor_resource_serving_bowl) <-> every AppleSliced piece's parentReceptacles contains the Bowl; inside(knife, drawer) <-> the Knife's parentReceptacles contains the Drawer; closed(drawer) <-> Drawer isOpen=false. Drawer is an iTHOR room-prefab part and Knife and Bowl are not primary objects in this part, so all three are planning resources. Knife safety: physical collection uses a pre-scored surrogate apple (for example foam wedges joined by weak magnets) with a blunt training knife; no sharp blade. Four wedges are the target, set by the surrogate's score lines.

tasks.name_en: Slice the potato, cook the slices in the pan on the front burner, then turn the burner off (simulation only)
tasks.name_ja: じゃがいもを切り、手前のコンロのフライパンで加熱してからコンロを消す（シミュレーションのみ）
instruction_variants: Slice the potato, put the knife back, cook all the slices in the pan on the front burner, and turn the burner off once they're cooked.
Make pan-cooked potato slices on the front burner and leave the stove off at the end.
じゃがいもを切って包丁を戻し、手前のコンロのフライパンで全部加熱してください。火が通ったらコンロを消してください。
tasks.notes: Workflow: three stages with checkpoints. Stage 1, slice and stow: the potato is sliced and the knife is back in its holder (checkpoint 1). Stage 2, cook: the slices are in the pan and the front burner is turned on until every slice reads cooked (checkpoint 2). Stage 3, shut off: the front knob is turned off and the burner reads off (checkpoint 3). Net changes are sliced, cooked, and inside(pan) on the potato; the burner goes off -> on -> off, so switched_off is a preserved end-state constraint reached through a transient articulation, and the knife's place in its holder is preserved. THOR mapping: sliced(thor_object_potato_1) <-> Potato isSliced=true (replaced by PotatoSliced pieces); cooked(thor_object_potato_1) <-> isCooked=true on every PotatoSliced piece; raw <-> isCooked=false; inside(..., thor_resource_frying_pan) <-> each piece's parentReceptacles contains the Pan; switched_off(thor_resource_stove_burner_front) <-> StoveBurner isToggled=false, which THOR drives through the paired StoveKnob; on_top_of(pan, burner) <-> the Pan's parentReceptacles contains the front StoveBurner. StoveBurner, StoveKnob, Pan, Knife, and the cutting board are planning resources (the first two are iTHOR room-prefab parts). Whether a toggled-on burner cooks items inside a pan on it, rather than only items directly on the burner, must be confirmed in the simulator (see the planning condition). The whole task is simulation-only: it uses a blade and a live heat source, and THOR's isCooked is not a model of real cooking. The stove-off end check is the same observation as the burner_knob_at_off_verified condition of thor_round1's pot task.

tasks.name_en: Clear the dining table: plate and cup into the sink, salt shaker back into its closed cabinet
tasks.name_ja: 食卓を片付ける：皿とコップは流しへ、塩入れは戸棚に戻して扉を閉める
instruction_variants: Clear the dining table: take the dirty plate and cup to the sink, put the salt shaker back in the spice cabinet, and close the cabinet.
After the meal, get everything off the table: dishes in the sink, salt in the cupboard, cupboard shut.
食卓を片付けてください。汚れた皿とコップは流しに、塩入れは調味料の戸棚に戻して扉を閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Workflow: two destinations in two stages with checkpoints. Stage 1, dishes: the dirty plate and the dirty cup go from the table into the sink basin (checkpoint 1: both in the basin, nothing broken). Stage 2, condiment: the cabinet is opened, the salt shaker stands upright inside, and the cabinet is closed (checkpoint 2). A final check confirms the table top is clear. Net changes are clear(table) and the three new locations; closed(cabinet) and switched_off(faucet) hold at both start and end and are preserved end-state constraints, and the dishes stay dirty because washing is out of scope. THOR mapping: clear(thor_object_dining_table_16_1) <-> the DiningTable's receptacleObjectIds is empty; inside(x, thor_resource_kitchen_sink_basin) <-> x's parentReceptacles contains the SinkBasin; inside(salt shaker, cabinet) <-> the SaltShaker's parentReceptacles contains the Cabinet; closed(cabinet) <-> Cabinet isOpen=false; switched_off(faucet) <-> Faucet isToggled=false; dirty <-> isDirty=true. Cross-link: the faucet is the thor_round1 ObjectInstance thor_object_kitchen_faucet_1 and is only checked, never used. The table sits in an eat-in kitchen within 3 m of the sink. Plate, Cup, and SaltShaker exist in the asset database but are not primary objects in this part; Cabinet and SinkBasin are iTHOR prefab parts; all are planning resources. Physical collection uses a shatter-proof plate and cup and a dry food-residue surrogate so nothing is spilled on the way.

tasks.name_en: Fish the TV remote out from between the sofa cushions and drop it in the remote basket
tasks.name_ja: ソファのクッションのすき間に落ちたテレビのリモコンを取り出し、リモコン用のかごに入れる
instruction_variants: The remote slipped down between the sofa cushions; put it in the basket on the coffee table.
Dig the TV remote out of the couch and drop it in its little basket.
ソファのすき間に落ちたリモコンを取り出して、ローテーブルのかごに入れてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the remote lies inside the remote basket; a reviewer sees the whole remote below the basket rim. Labelled atomic: one object and one net change (wedged in the cushion gap -> inside the basket) in one uninterrupted reach, pull, and drop. The retrieval from a partly hidden, compliant gap is what separates this from a plain relocation; the basket staying on the coffee table is a preserved constraint, not a goal change. THOR mapping: inside(remote, basket) <-> the remote's parentReceptacles include the basket receptacle (a Bowl or Box stands in, since THOR has no basket type); wedged_in has no THOR equivalent because the Sofa asset has no cushion gaps, so the start pose is a planning condition and an asset_compatibility limitation. The remote's buttons are not pressed and the television is out of scope.

tasks.name_en: Set the phone face up on the bedside charging pad so the charge light comes on (dummy pad)
tasks.name_ja: スマートフォンを枕元の充電パッドに画面を上にして置き、充電ランプを点ける（ダミーパッド）
instruction_variants: Put the phone on the charging pad on the nightstand.
Take the phone off the bed and lay it screen-up on the wireless charger so the light comes on.
ベッドの上のスマホを、ナイトテーブルの充電パッドに画面を上にして置いてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the phone lies face up on the charging pad and the pad's charge light is on; the light is the observable test that the phone is aligned. Labelled atomic: one object and one net change (not charging -> charging), reached by one pick, orient, and aligned place; on_top_of is the relation that produces the charging state, not a separate goal. Power policy: the pad is a battery-powered dummy with a magnet-triggered indicator (a small magnet taped to the back of a decommissioned phone or phone dummy). No real charging takes place, and the lit indicator stands in for charging. THOR mapping: THOR has no charger objectType and no charging state. isToggled on the CellPhone is a screen flag and must not be read as charging; on_top_of(phone, pad) can only be checked as parentReceptacles including the SideTable with the phone inside a marked 9 x 17 cm footprint. The uncertain mapping is a planning condition and an asset_compatibility limitation.

tasks.name_en: Lift the potted plant off the mopped floor and set it back upright, centred on its drip saucer
tasks.name_ja: 床掃除のためにどけた鉢植えを持ち上げ、受け皿の中央にまっすぐ戻す
instruction_variants: Put the plant back on its saucer by the window.
Lift the potted plant and set it squarely in the middle of the drip tray without spilling soil.
鉢植えを窓際の受け皿の真ん中に戻してください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the potted plant stands on its drip saucer, centred and upright; a reviewer sees the pot base inside the saucer rim with an even margin. Labelled atomic: one object and one net change (floor -> saucer) in a single lift and place. upright holds at the start as well, so it is a preserved end-state constraint with a tolerance, not a second goal change. The task is placement with a centring tolerance on a heavy, top-heavy object, which is why it is kept as a task rather than a bare relocation. It differs from task_thor_r1_watering_can_fill_water_plant_return, which waters a plant and leaves it in place; no water is used here. THOR mapping: on_top_of(plant, saucer) <-> the HousePlant's parentReceptacles include the saucer receptacle (a Plate stands in, as THOR has no saucer type); upright <-> the plant's rotation within 5 degrees of vertical. HousePlant is Moveable, not CanPickup, so THOR cannot lift it; simulated goal checks need a teleport or push, which is a planning condition and an asset_compatibility limitation. isFilledWithLiquid is not part of the goal.

tasks.name_en: Pack the three CD cases from the TV stand into the cardboard box and fold its flaps shut
tasks.name_ja: テレビ台の上のCDケース3枚を段ボール箱に詰め、フラップを折って閉じる
instruction_variants: Put the three CDs in the box and close it.
Pack the CD cases off the TV stand into the cardboard box, then fold the four flaps down.
テレビ台のCDケースを3枚とも段ボール箱に入れて、ふたを閉じてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the three CD cases are inside the box and the box is closed with all four flaps folded down. Labelled compound: four goal predicate changes (three inside, one closed) across four objects in one sitting. THOR mapping: inside(cd, box) <-> each CD's parentReceptacles include the Box; open/closed <-> Box isOpen true/false. The database's 'open' state has the same bounding box as the default, so the flap pose behind isOpen is not recorded and must be confirmed in the simulator before a simulated closed check is trusted. Physical closed is defined as all four flaps folded to within 15 degrees of horizontal and not interlocked (tuck-folding is out of scope).

tasks.name_en: Close the book left open on the armchair and stand it upright back on the bookshelf
tasks.name_ja: 肘掛け椅子の上に開いたまま置かれた本を閉じ、本棚に立てて戻す
instruction_variants: Close the book on the armchair and put it back on the shelf.
Shut the open book and stand it up on the bookshelf, spine facing out.
肘掛け椅子で開いたままの本を閉じて、背表紙を手前にして本棚に立ててください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the book is closed and stands upright on the middle shelf, spine out, in the marked gap. Labelled compound: three goal predicate changes on one object (closed, on the shelf, upright where it started lying flat) in one sitting. THOR mapping: open/closed <-> Book isOpen true/false (the database's 'open' box is twice as wide, 0.85 m vs 0.43 m, consistent with a spread-open book); on_top_of(book, shelf) <-> parentReceptacles include the ShelvingUnit; upright has no THOR state and is checked as the book's rotation within 10 degrees of vertical with the spine facing out. THOR may not keep a book standing without neighbours, so the neighbouring books are resources and the simulated upright check is a planning condition. It differs from task_gso_r1_bookends_four_books_upright, which stands four books between bookends; here one open book is closed and returned.

tasks.name_en: Pick the worn T-shirt and socks off the bedroom floor, drop them in the hamper, and close its lid
tasks.name_ja: 寝室の床に脱ぎ捨てたTシャツと靴下を拾って洗濯かごに入れ、ふたを閉める
instruction_variants: Put the clothes on the floor in the hamper and shut the lid.
Pick up the T-shirt and the socks, drop them in the laundry basket, and close it.
床に脱いだTシャツと靴下を洗濯かごに入れて、ふたを閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the T-shirt and both socks are inside the hamper and its lid is closed; a reviewer sees nothing of either garment outside the hamper or under the lid edge. Labelled compound: two net changes (two garments inside) plus a transient articulation that must be reversed (open the lid, then close it again). closed holds at both start and end, so it is a preserved end-state constraint, not a goal change. Cross-link: the T-shirt is the YCB object ycb_074_t_shirt, used here as a worn garment; the socks are a planning resource. THOR mapping: open/closed <-> LaundryHamper isOpen true/false (the 'open' box is taller, 0.85 m vs 0.60 m, consistent with a raised lid); inside <-> each garment's parentReceptacles include the hamper (THOR objectType Cloth stands in for both garments, and is rigid). The garments are not folded; their shape is not part of the goal.

tasks.name_en: Reset the sofa for the evening: pillows back at both arms, blanket folded over the right arm, laptop closed on the coffee table
tasks.name_ja: 夜に向けてソファを整える：クッションを両端に戻し、ブランケットをたたんで右の肘掛けに掛け、ノートパソコンを閉じてローテーブルに置く
instruction_variants: Tidy the sofa: pillows up, blanket folded, laptop closed on the table.
Put both cushions back against the backrest at the ends, fold the throw over the right arm, and shut the laptop and move it to the coffee table.
ソファを片付けてください。クッションは両端に立てて、ブランケットはたたんで右の肘掛けに、ノートパソコンは閉じてローテーブルへ。
tasks.notes: Goal: the sofa seat is free for sitting; both pillows stand against the backrest at the two ends, the blanket is folded and draped over the right arm, and the laptop is closed on the coffee table. Labelled workflow: three stages with a checkpoint after each (laptop off the seat first, then the blanket fold, then the pillows) and three destinations (coffee table, sofa arm, sofa ends). Goal changes: closed and relocated laptop, folded and relocated blanket, two pillows relocated and turned upright. Cross-link: the laptop is thor_object_laptop_1 from thor_round1; its closing and move to the coffee table repeat the goal of task_thor_r1_laptop_close_to_coffee_table as one stage of a larger reset, and the laptop is cleared first so the blanket and pillows are not handled over it. THOR mapping: on_top_of(x, sofa) <-> parentReceptacles include the Sofa; closed(laptop) <-> Laptop isOpen=false; on_top_of(laptop, coffee table) <-> parentReceptacles include the CoffeeTable. upright for the pillows is judged by the pillow's broad face standing within 20 degrees of the backrest; THOR Pillow has no pose state. folded and draped_over have no THOR equivalent (THOR has no blanket type and no cloth simulation), so they are physical-only checks; this is a planning condition and an asset_compatibility limitation.

tasks.name_en: Bin the old newspaper, take the full living-room liner to the kitchen garbage can, and fit a fresh liner
tasks.name_ja: 古新聞をリビングのゴミ箱に捨て、いっぱいになった袋を台所のゴミ箱へ運び、新しい袋をかける
instruction_variants: Throw out the newspaper and empty the living-room bin into the kitchen bin.
Put yesterday's paper in the little bin, tie off the bag, take it to the kitchen garbage, and put a new bag in.
古新聞をゴミ箱に入れて、袋を縛って台所のゴミ箱に捨て、新しい袋をかけておいてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the newspaper is in the used liner, the liner is tied and inside the closed kitchen garbage can, and the living-room waste basket holds a fresh liner with its rim folded over. Labelled workflow: four stages across two rooms with a checkpoint after each (newspaper binned; liner tied and lifted out; liner in the kitchen can with the lid closed; fresh liner fitted) and two destinations (kitchen can, living-room basket). closed(kitchen can) holds at start and end and is a preserved constraint reached through a transient open. Cross-link: the living-room bin is gso_object_waste_basket (8.5 L); fitting its fresh liner repeats the goal of task_gso_r1_waste_basket_replace_liner as the last stage of a longer multi-room chain. THOR mapping: inside(newspaper, bag) <-> the newspaper's parentReceptacles include the GarbageCan that stands in for the basket; THOR has no liner, bag, or tie state, so tied, the bag's move to the kitchen can, and the fresh liner are physical-only checks. closed(kitchen can) has no THOR state because GarbageCan is not CanOpen; it is a physical lidded can. These gaps are planning conditions and an asset_compatibility limitation.

tasks.name_en: Shut the dripping bathroom sink faucet until no drop falls for 30 seconds
tasks.name_ja: ぽたぽた垂れている洗面台の蛇口を30秒間しずくが落ちなくなるまで閉める
instruction_variants: The bathroom tap is dripping; shut it off properly.
Push the sink faucet lever fully to its off stop so it stops dripping.
洗面台の蛇口から水が垂れているので、しずくが止まるまでしっかり閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one fixture and one net change (a partly open, dripping faucet -> fully off). dripping(...) describes the start only and is not a goal predicate. Differs from task_thor_r1_shower_switch_off: the start state is a slow drip, not a running stream, so the end state is judged by a 30-second no-drop window rather than by a visible stream stopping, and the control is a single sink lever. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: switched_on/switched_off <-> Faucet isToggled true/false on Bathroom_Faucet_1. THOR has no partly-open or drip state, so the dripping start is represented as isToggled=true; this mapping is recorded as the planning condition thor_faucet_drip_represented_as_istoggled_true and in the asset_compatibility limitation. Reuses template_thor_switch_device_off from thor_round1.

tasks.name_en: Hang the bath towel over the towel bar with both sides level and clear of the floor
tasks.name_ja: バスタオルをタオル掛けに左右の丈をそろえて床につかないように掛ける
instruction_variants: Hang the bath towel on the towel bar.
Drape the towel over the bar so the front and back hang to the same length.
バスタオルをタオル掛けに、前後の長さがそろうように掛けてください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one object and one net change (folded on the counter -> hanging over the bar); the evenness tolerances define what counts as hanging_on and are not extra goal predicates. The towel starts folded in half lengthwise and stays folded lengthwise over the bar; folded is a start description, not a goal change. Differs from task_gso_r2_hand_towel_hang_on_ring: a full bath towel draped over a straight bar, with front and back hem levels, instead of a hand towel pulled through a ring. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: hanging_on(towel, bar) <-> the Towel's parentReceptacles contains the TowelHolder (e.g. Bath_Towel_Holder1, an ObjectSpecificReceptacle). THOR snaps the towel to a fixed pose, so hem levels and floor clearance are physical checks only; the bar is a planning resource because it is not a primary object of this part.

tasks.name_en: Move the plunger from the bath mat into its holder cup beside the toilet
tasks.name_ja: バスマットの上のラバーカップをトイレ横の専用ホルダーに立てて戻す
instruction_variants: Put the plunger back in its holder next to the toilet.
The plunger is standing on the bath mat; stand it back in the cup by the toilet.
バスマットの上に置かれたラバーカップを、トイレの横のホルダーに立てて戻してください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one object and one net change (on the bath mat -> inside the holder cup) in a single carry-and-lower motion. upright holds at both start and end (the plunger starts standing on its cup on the mat), so it is a preserved end-state constraint, not a goal change. Cross-link: the holder stands beside thor_object_toilet_1 (thor_round1); the toilet is a landmark only and its lid state is not part of this task. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: inside <-> the Plunger's parentReceptacles contains the holder; THOR has no plunger-holder object, so a simulated check uses a floor position within 15 cm of the toilet base instead; upright has no THOR state and is judged from the handle axis. Real collection uses a new, never-used plunger.

tasks.name_en: Replace the empty toilet-paper core on the hanger with a fresh roll and bin the core
tasks.name_ja: ペーパーホルダーの空の芯を新しいトイレットペーパーに替え、芯をごみ箱に捨てる
instruction_variants: The toilet roll has run out; put a new one on and throw the old core away.
Take the empty core off the holder, bin it, and mount the fresh roll from the tank lid.
トイレットペーパーがなくなったので、芯をごみ箱に捨てて新しいロールをホルダーに付けてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: two net changes over two objects in one sitting (the fresh roll becomes mounted on the hanger; the spent core goes into the garbage can), plus a transient articulation that must be reversed (the spring spindle or swing arm is removed or opened, then re-seated). used_up on the core is an invariant that tells it apart from the fresh roll. Differs from task_thor_r1_paper_towel_spent_roll_discard (kitchen, discard only): this task also restocks the holder. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: mounted_on(roll, hanger) <-> the ToiletPaper's parentReceptacles contains the ToiletPaperHanger (e.g. Toilet_Paper_Hanger_1, an ObjectSpecificReceptacle); used_up <-> isUsedUp=true (Toilet_Paper_Used_Up is the database's bare-core asset); inside(core, can) <-> the core's parentReceptacles contains the GarbageCan. THOR has no spindle, so the spindle step has no simulated counterpart. The hanger, core, tank lid, and can are planning resources.

tasks.name_en: Refill the empty hand-soap pump bottle to its fill line from the refill jug and screw the pump back on
tasks.name_ja: 空のハンドソープのポンプボトルに詰め替え容器から目盛りまで補充し、ポンプを締め直す
instruction_variants: The hand soap is empty; refill it from the refill jug.
Unscrew the pump, pour from the refill jug up to the line, and screw the pump back on.
ハンドソープが空なので、詰め替え容器から目盛りまで入れてポンプを締め直してください。
tasks.notes: Compound: one net change (empty -> full to the line) plus two transient articulations that must be reversed (pump head unscrewed then re-seated; jug cap opened then recapped), over two objects in one sitting. lid_seated and capped hold at both start and end, so they are preserved end-state constraints, not goal changes; the bottle stays on the spill tray throughout. Surrogate: real soap is a slip hazard and hard to clean between trials, so the jug holds water tinted with food colouring; full means the liquid surface is within 1 cm below the marked fill line. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: empty/full <-> SoapBottle isUsedUp true/false. THOR's SoapBottle has CanBeUsedUp but not CanBeFilled, and no pump part; whether isUsedUp can be reset to false by any action has not been confirmed, so this is the planning condition thor_soapbottle_usedup_reset_confirmed_in_simulator and an asset_compatibility limitation. The jug, pump head, and tray are planning resources.

tasks.name_en: Close the vanity cabinet, vanity drawer, toilet lid, and bathroom door that were left open
tasks.name_ja: 開けっぱなしの洗面台下の扉、洗面台の引き出し、便器のふた、浴室のドアをすべて閉める
instruction_variants: Everything in the bathroom was left open; close the cabinet, the drawer, the toilet lid, and the door.
Shut the under-sink cabinet and the vanity drawer, lower the toilet lid, then close the bathroom door on your way out.
浴室で開いたままの洗面台下の扉、引き出し、便器のふたを閉め、最後に出るときにドアを閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: four closed goal predicates on four openables in one room and one sitting; no stage needs a reset or a checkpoint beyond the final check, so it is not a workflow. The scope is exactly these four items, not every openable in the house. Order: the three inside items first, then the door from the hallway side; the robot's final position is not part of the goal state. Cross-link and overlap: the toilet is thor_object_toilet_1 (thor_round1); lowering its lid alone is task_thor_r1_toilet_lid_close, and this task has a wider scope. The under-sink cabinet door resource matches task_thor_r1_spray_bottle_return_under_sink. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: open/closed = isOpen on the Doorway (Doorway_1), the Toilet, and the vanity Cabinet and Drawer room parts. ProcTHOR sets doorway openness at house generation; whether Close/OpenObject act on a generated doorway and which pose isOpen=true denotes is unconfirmed, so it is the planning condition thor_doorway_isopen_confirmed_in_simulator and an asset_compatibility limitation.

tasks.name_en: Collect the dirty cloths from the kitchen counter and the bathroom floor into the bedroom laundry hamper and close its lid
tasks.name_ja: キッチンの台と浴室の床にある汚れたふきんを寝室の洗濯かごに集めてふたを閉める
instruction_variants: Gather the dirty cloths from the kitchen and the bathroom and put them in the bedroom hamper.
Pick up the cloth on the kitchen counter, then the one on the bathroom floor, drop both in the laundry hamper, and close the lid.
キッチンと浴室の汚れたふきんを集めて寝室の洗濯かごに入れ、ふたを閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Workflow: three stages in three rooms (kitchen pickup, bathroom pickup, bedroom deposit) with a checkpoint after each pickup that the source spot is clear and the cloth is still held; two net changes (both cloths inside the hamper) plus a transient articulation (hamper lid opened then closed). closed on the hamper and dirty on both cloths hold at start and end and are preserved constraints, not goal changes; nothing is washed. Differs from task_gso_r2_kitchen_towels_swap_for_fresh_pack (one kitchen, swap for fresh towels) and task_thor_r1_washing_machine_load_start (loading the machine): here the goal is collecting from two rooms into a lidded hamper in a third. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: dirty <-> Cloth isDirty=true; inside <-> each cloth's parentReceptacles contains the LaundryHamper; open/closed <-> LaundryHamper isOpen (Laundry_Hamper_1_1 has Receptacle and CanOpen). The hamper is a planning resource here; part B of this round declares thor_object_laundry_hamper_1_1 (Laundry_Hamper_1_1), which can be bound in its place at merge. Part B's task_thor_r2_hamper_floor_clothes_lid_closed (bedroom floor clothes, one room, compound) uses the same hamper with a different scope.

tasks.name_en: Empty the bathroom and bedroom wastebaskets into one garbage bag, tie it, and set it by the front door
tasks.name_ja: 浴室と寝室のごみ箱の中身を一つのごみ袋にまとめて口を縛り、玄関の横に置く
instruction_variants: Collect the bathroom and bedroom trash into one bag and leave it by the front door.
Take the open bag from the kitchen, tip both wastebaskets into it, put each basket back, tie the bag, and set it beside the front door.
浴室と寝室のごみ箱の中身を一つの袋に集め、袋の口を縛って玄関の横に置いてください。
tasks.notes: Workflow: four stages at four places (kitchen bag pickup, bathroom bin, bedroom bin, front door) with a checkpoint after each bin that it is empty and back on its floor mark; four goal predicates (two bins empty, bag closed, bag at the front-door spot). Each bin is lifted and returned, a transient move that must be reversed; its floor position is a preserved constraint. Scope: exactly these two wastebaskets and one bag; the kitchen bin is not part of the task. Differs from part B's task_thor_r2_newspaper_bin_empty_to_kitchen_can (one living-room liner to the kitchen can, with a fresh liner fitted): here two rooms' bins are consolidated into one bag left at the exit. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: empty(bin) <-> the GarbageCan's receptacleObjectIds is empty; at(bag, spot) <-> the GarbageBag position within 50 cm of the marked spot. GarbageBag_21_1 has only the Moveable flag (no Receptacle, no CanOpen), so THOR cannot put litter inside the bag or represent tied/untied; open/closed on the bag and the litter ending up in the bag are physical checks only. This is the planning condition thor_garbagebag_contents_and_tie_not_simulated and an asset_compatibility limitation. Bins, spots, and litter are planning resources.

draft_notes: thor_round2: 24 tasks on 24 further AI2-THOR / ProcTHOR assets (9 atomic, 9 compound, 6 workflow) across kitchen, living room, bedroom, bathroom, and multi-room contexts, drafted by three claude-opus-5-5 subagents with the thor_round1 review lessons applied, and merged.

thor_round2 part A: eight kitchen tasks anchored to AI2-THOR / ProcTHOR assets Fridge_1, Egg_1, coffee_machine_1, Lettuce_1, Kettle_1, Apple_1, Potato_1, and Dining_Table_16_1, drafted from data/research/thor_candidates.json (3 atomic, 3 compound, 2 workflow).

Evidence evidence_thor_task_design_round2 is defined in the skeleton data/drafts/thor_round2.json; catalog_identity claims cite the existing active evidence_procthor_asset_database from thor_round1. Neither is redefined here, and no scenes are added.

Asset IDs, objectTypes, state flags, split values, and bounding boxes were checked against the asset database at commit d4c4c6a9fdd9679c8b9343d771c510016cd310df on 2026-09-25. None of the eight assets is an ObjectInstance in an active bundle or in Lane A's reference_gso_round1.json.

State changes new to the THOR bundles: a refrigerator door and a fridge shelf placement, a coffee machine off-check with a mug in its slot, a cracked egg, a lidded kettle filled, an apple sliced into a bowl with the knife stowed, a potato sliced and pan-cooked with the burner off, and a dining table cleared to two destinations.

Cross-links to thor_round1 ObjectInstances: thor_object_mug_1 (coffee machine task) and thor_object_kitchen_faucet_1 (kettle and dining-table tasks). thor_object_fridge_1 anchors the ajar-door task and is bound in the lettuce task.

Resource IDs beginning thor_resource_ are planning object requirements, not ObjectInstances. New resources: fridge door swing path, fridge middle shelf, mixing bowl, coffee machine power button, serving bowl, cutlery drawer, frying pan, front stove burner and knob, dirty plate, dirty cup, salt shaker, spice cabinet. Reused from thor_round1: counter work zone, kitchen sink basin, knife or blunt surrogate, cutting board, guarded knife holder.

Safety: the egg and potato tasks are simulation-only (raw egg; blade plus live heat). The apple task uses a pre-scored surrogate with a blunt training knife. The coffee machine is unplugged with a battery dummy indicator that stands in for power, and the mug holds room-temperature water. The kettle task is wet and declares robot_electronics_splash_protected. Fridge tasks declare a clear hinge-side pinch zone.

Uncertain THOR mappings are planning conditions and asset_compatibility limitations: Fridge_1 door count, Fridge_1 shelf sub-receptacles, the egg crack action (SliceObject vs BreakObject), whether the Kettle fills with its lid closed, whether a burner cooks items inside a pan, the front knob-burner pairing, and ProcTHOR decor on the dining table.

Concepts: object_kitchen_appliance, object_food_item, object_furniture, object_cookware, and object_fruit already exist; object_vegetable (lettuce, potato) is new, as proposed in thor_candidates.json.

Eight new templates (template_thor_r2a_*). The round-1 slice and load-appliance templates were not reused because their goals differ (slices stay on the board; the item goes into a switched-off heating appliance).

Part B of thor_round2 (8 tasks: 3 atomic, 3 compound, 2 workflow): living-room and bedroom tidy-ups and state changes anchored to AI2-THOR / ProcTHOR assets Remote_1, Cellphone_3, Houseplant_1, Box_1, Book_1, Laundry_Hamper_1_1, RoboTHOR_sofa_kramfors, and Newspaper_1, drafted from data/research/thor_candidates.json.

Scenes (scene_home_living_room, scene_home_bedroom, scene_multi_room_house) come from thor_round1. evidence_thor_task_design_round2 is defined in the skeleton data/drafts/thor_round2.json and evidence_procthor_asset_database in thor_round1; neither is redefined here, and no per-object evidence is created.

Asset IDs, objectTypes, state flags, bounding boxes, and scene listings were checked against the asset database at commit d4c4c6a9fdd9679c8b9343d771c510016cd310df on 2026-09-25. RoboTHOR_sofa_kramfors was chosen over the candidate RoboTHOR_sofa_ektorp_v because ektorp lists no scenes.

Cross-links: thor_object_laptop_1 (thor_round1) in the sofa reset; ycb_074_t_shirt as the worn T-shirt in the hamper task; gso_object_waste_basket (gso_round1) as the living-room bin in the bin-emptying workflow. Overlaps with task_thor_r1_laptop_close_to_coffee_table and task_gso_r1_waste_basket_replace_liner are single stages of larger workflows and are stated in the task notes.

Resource IDs beginning thor_resource_ are planning object requirements (cushion gap, basket, charging pad, saucer, CD cases, shelf, socks, pillows, blanket, liners, kitchen can), not cataloged ObjectInstances.
Proposed new Atlas concept: object_plant (houseplant). The other objects reuse object_electronic_device, object_receptacle, object_paper_item, and object_furniture.

Power policy: the only powered device is the phone, a decommissioned phone or dummy on a battery dummy charging pad whose magnet-triggered indicator stands in for charging; the laptop is decommissioned or a dummy with no charger. No task uses water.

Uncertain THOR mappings are planning conditions and asset_compatibility limitations: no cushion gaps on Sofa; no charging state (CellPhone isToggled is not charging); HousePlant is Moveable, not CanPickup; Box 'open' state records no geometry; no book upright state; no blanket, cloth fold, bin liner, or lidded GarbageCan.
Eight new templates with the template_thor_r2b_ prefix, one per task.

thor_round2 part C (8 tasks: 3 atomic, 3 compound, 2 workflow): bathroom sink faucet, bath towel, plunger, toilet paper, soap bottle refill, bathroom openables with Doorway_1, and two multi-room workflows (dirty cloths to the bedroom hamper; two wastebaskets into one garbage bag by the front door). Drafted from data/research/thor_candidates.json bathroom and multi_room candidates.

Scenes and evidence are not redefined here: evidence_thor_task_design_round2 comes from the skeleton data/drafts/thor_round2.json, evidence_procthor_asset_database and scene_multi_room_house from thor_round1, and scene_home_bathroom from gso_round1.

Asset IDs, objectTypes, bounding boxes, and state flags were checked against the asset database at commit d4c4c6a9fdd9679c8b9343d771c510016cd310df on 2026-09-25. None of the eight assets is an ObjectInstance in an active bundle.

Only the primary asset of each task is an ObjectInstance (thor_object_<asset slug>). Supporting items (towel bar, holder cup, hanger, spent core, refill jug, pump head, cabinet door, drawer, hamper, wastebaskets, spots) are thor_resource_* planning object requirements, not ObjectInstances or claims that matching assets exist. The hamper stays a resource so a hamper ObjectInstance from another part can be bound at merge.

Cross-links: thor_object_toilet_1 (thor_round1) is the landmark in the plunger task and one of the four openables in the close-everything task. task_thor_r2_bathroom_sink_faucet_drip_off reuses template_thor_switch_device_off from thor_round1.

Uncertain THOR mappings are planning conditions and asset_compatibility limitations: thor_faucet_drip_represented_as_istoggled_true, thor_soapbottle_usedup_reset_confirmed_in_simulator, thor_doorway_isopen_confirmed_in_simulator, thor_garbagebag_contents_and_tie_not_simulated.

No new Atlas concepts: object_home_fixture (faucet, doorway), object_textile (towel, cloth), object_cleaning_tool (plunger), object_paper_item (toilet paper), object_personal_care_container (hand-soap bottle), object_receptacle (garbage bag).
Seven new templates (template_thor_r2c_*); each lists the scenes it is used in.
Merge: the two-room cloth workflow now binds part B's thor_object_laundry_hamper_1_1 instead of a separate hamper resource.
